body.prompt: Close-up inside a small busy Korean restaurant: young people's hands holding chopsticks over bowls of fiery red spicy braised chicken, one hand wiping sweat with a paper napkin, glasses of water, steam; faces out of frame.
A long instant noodle factory production line with countless plain red noodle packets moving along a conveyor belt into the distance, workers in white caps far away, warm industrial light.
Dramatic close-up of a single plain glossy red instant noodle packet with flame-like shapes and no readable label, lying on a dark wooden table, a few dried chili peppers beside it.
Black-and-white archival film look, 1960s: a huge steaming iron pot in a market alley, a hand ladling thin porridge into a tin bowl held out by another hand, rough clothes, film grain.
Black-and-white archival look, 1963 Korea: an early noodle factory where workers in white caps watch a simple machine fold blocks of fried noodles onto metal trays, steam and film grain.
1970s Korean neighborhood corner shop: wooden shelves stacked high with plain instant noodle packets, a child buying one, faded warm sepia colors.
1970s Korea sepia photograph look: a small school-side snack bar where students in uniforms eat noodles at long wooden tables, steam rising, posters with no readable text.
1989: a hand turning a large old newspaper with a huge blurred headline block and a grainy photo of noodle packets, on a kitchen table, autumn light; no readable text.
An industrial oil refinery yard with large storage tanks and pipes at grey dusk, cold mood, a chain-link fence in the foreground.
A dim warehouse piled to the ceiling with returned cardboard boxes of instant noodles, a single forklift standing still, a stopped conveyor belt, cold blue light.
The exterior of a large stone Korean supreme court building with tall columns under an overcast sky, empty wide steps, years later mood.
1997: a dark empty office at night, desks piled with stacks of documents and unpaid bills, a single desk lamp on, rain on the window, the city lights outside dim.

A Korean supermarket instant noodle aisle: the middle eye-level shelves are full of colorful competitor noodle packets, while a few plain older-looking packets sit alone on the bottom shelf; no labels readable.
Seen from behind: a woman in a plain dark coat opening the door to an empty company meeting room with a long table and dusty chairs, morning light through the blinds.
Before dawn: a frosted window of an old noodle factory, a lone woman walking toward the factory gate under a street light, breath visible, winter.
A store shelf where several new instant noodle packets in different colors sit, some already marked down with blank stickers, half-empty spaces between them; no readable labels.
A large hand-drawn paper map of South Korea spread on a desk, many small red pins stuck into cities, a notebook and chili peppers beside it, top-down view.
Mid-2000s night street in a Seoul nightlife district: many small restaurants with glowing red flame-shaped signs with no readable letters, crowds of young people, smoke from grills.
Extreme close-up of a kitchen knife slicing small green and red Korean chili peppers on a wooden cutting board, seeds scattered, dramatic light.
2012: a hand placing the first plain red instant noodle packet with flame drawings onto a convenience store shelf, bright fluorescent light, no readable text.
Night outside a Korean convenience store: three friends seen from behind at a plastic outdoor table sharing one bowl of fiery red noodles, one fanning their mouth, cans of milk on the table.
Close-up of chopsticks lifting creamy orange-pink spicy noodles from a bowl, glossy sauce, melted cheese threads, soft warm light.
A smartphone held in a hand showing a blurred video of people reacting to very spicy noodles with tears and waving hands, the faces blurred and unrecognizable, a dark room lit by the screen.
A vintage world map on paper where red ink dots spread outward from Korea across Asia, North America and Europe like drops of chili sauce, top-down view.
A busy Korean container port at golden hour, stacks of red and navy shipping containers, a huge cargo ship being loaded by cranes.
Aerial view of a large new modern food factory with white roofs among green rice fields and low mountains in southern Korea, morning mist.
A large American big-box supermarket aisle of instant noodles, bright lights, a shopping cart in the foreground, red noodle packets stacked at eye level on the main shelf; labels unreadable.
A wall of many small TV screens in a grid showing different news studios and anchors from around the world, all faces blurred, each screen showing a red noodle packet graphic with no text.

The same narrow Myeongdong alley in Seoul at night, now full of foreign tourists and locals lining up in front of a small glowing spicy food restaurant, neon reflections on wet pavement, warm and lively.
An empty snack shelf in a Korean convenience store with a single handwritten blank paper note taped to it, a few crumbs, no readable text, slightly melancholic light.
Stacks of cardboard export boxes with red flame drawings on pallets in a bright modern warehouse, shipping labels blank, a forklift moving a pallet toward a loading dock.
A quiet meeting table with an open investment report folder, a cup of coffee, a pen, and a single red noodle packet placed beside the documents, late afternoon window light.
A neat close-up of US dollar bills and Korean won bills fanned out on a desk next to a calculator, soft light; no readable text.
A food lab bench with several unmarked prototype noodle packets in new colors, small tasting bowls and a researcher's hand writing in a notebook.
